name: What bathroom fixtures are cheapest to relocate: sink, shower, or toilet?

mainEntity.name: What bathroom fixtures are cheapest to relocate: sink, shower, or toilet?
mainEntity.text: What bathroom fixtures are cheapest to relocate: sink, shower, or toilet?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most bathroom remodels, the sink or vanity is the least expensive fixture to relocate because its plumbing is simpler and usually easier to access. A shower is more expensive because the drain, trap, and waterproofing all have to be rebuilt around the new position. A toilet is often the most costly move because the waste line is larger, the venting is more sensitive, and slab or framing work can become extensive. The distance of the move matters, but access matters just as much. A short toilet move through a slab can cost more than a longer vanity move through an open wall. For budgeting, it helps to think in terms of complexity rather than fixture count. If the goal is to control cost, keeping the toilet close to the existing drain and moving sinks first is usually the most efficient layout strategy.
acceptedAnswer.description: A sink or vanity is usually the cheapest fixture to move, followed by a shower, with a toilet typically the most expensive. The toilet costs more because the drain diameter, vent tie-in, and slope requirements are harder to reroute than supply lines alone.
